pattern_definition.name: Plan Task to Super-Atomic Step Transformation
pattern_definition.description: A systematic decomposition process that converts human-level plan tasks into maximally atomic, machine-dispatchable steps with single operations and precise I/O contracts.

source_perspective.viewpoint: Human planner perspective - holistic objective with flexible scope

characteristics.char: Context references can be general ("relevant docs")
Verification criteria often subjective ("quality looks good")

target_perspective.viewpoint: Machine execution perspective - precise operations with verifiable outcomes

characteristics.char: Single objective per step (e.g., "Add section X to file Y at line Z")
Specific files only, no directory globs or general references
Precise context inputs with file:line citations where applicable
Concrete verification criteria using grep/file state checks

rule.name: Objective Granularity Refinement
rule.after: Super-Atomic step states exactly how and where:

rule.name: Files In Scope Specialization
rule.before: Directory references or glob patterns allowed:
rule.after: Must list specific file paths only (tasks/abc.md, not tasks/*.md):

rule.name: Context Minimization Enforcement
rule.after: Cite specific artifacts with line/section references when possible:

rule.name: Deterministic Verification Requirement
rule.after: Concrete checks using grep, file state assertions, or automated scripts:

source_plan_task.title: Document Super-Atomic Pattern
source_plan_task.original_objective: Create visual diagram showing decomposition flow from plan tasks to super-atomic steps.

context_package.files_out_of_scope_reference: Task context explicitly excludes other reference files not needed for this diagram creation.

step.verification: Transformation pattern file exists with valid XML syntax and mermaid mindmap content present.
index.xml contains item referencing transformation-pattern.xml with correct path and type.

constraints.constraint: Each super-atomic step must route to exactly one worker skill family
No compound multi-file changes listed as single action item
Context inputs must cite specific artifacts, never broad directory references
Dependencies reference specific step outputs, not vague phase names
